hero.headline: U.S. launches second night of airstrikes on Iran to pressure nuclear deal
hero.body:
The U.S. military struck targets in Iran for the second consecutive night, with officials stating the intent was to pressure Tehran to sign a nuclear agreement. The strikes carry the risk of escalating military conflict between the two countries.

U.S. officials said they expected an Iranian response, similar to what occurred after the first round of strikes. Tehran announced its military had targeted the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet in Bahrain with drones in response to the latest American strikes, though it was not immediately clear whether the attack succeeded.

The sequential nights of bombing represent an intensification of U.S. military action against Iran. Officials framed the operation as part of a strategy to bring Iran to the negotiating table for an agreement, though the approach risks provoking further retaliation against American forces in the region.

The 5th Fleet, headquartered in Bahrain, oversees U.S. naval operations in the Persian Gulf, Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and parts of the Indian Ocean. Iranian drone attacks targeting the fleet would represent a direct military response to American forces, raising the prospect of an expanding conflict. U.S. bases in the region have previously been targeted by Iranian forces and allied militias.

The back-and-forth strikes mark a significant moment in U.S.-Iran relations, with both countries engaged in direct military action against each other. The outcome of the pressure campaign remains uncertain, as does Iran's capacity and willingness to continue retaliatory strikes against American military installations in response to the ongoing air operations.

cards.headline: US inflation rises at fastest pace in three years
cards.body:
Consumer prices in the United States are rising at the fastest rate in three years, according to new economic data released this week. The personal consumption expenditures price index jumped 3.8% in the 12 months through April, marking the largest increase since May 2023.

The acceleration in inflation reflects multiple pressures on the economy. The Middle East conflict has disrupted shipping routes and global supply chains, pushing energy prices higher. The national average retail gasoline price shot up 12.3% in April alone, with gasoline prices climbing more than 50% since the war began at the end of February. Beyond energy, consumers are also paying more for food, goods, and services across the board.

Inflation was already elevated before the war, largely due to Trump's sweeping import duties. Goods prices increased 0.7% in April, with food prices rebounding 0.5%. Services prices, including housing, utilities, and food services, also rose. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy components, increased 3.3% year-on-year in April after rising 3.2% in March.

The rising prices are taking a toll on American households. Real income at the disposal of households, adjusted for inflation, dropped for a third straight month in April. Consumer spending patterns are shifting as families adjust budgets to accommodate higher costs. Consumers are depleting savings to maintain spending levels, with the saving rate dropping to 2.6% in April, the lowest level since June 2022.

The inflation surge comes as President Trump faces growing political challenges. Americans are increasingly frustrated with his handling of the economy. A Reuters and Ipsos survey showed the president's approval rating fell to nearly its lowest level since returning to the White House, hurt by a drop in support among Republicans. Trump won the 2024 presidential election largely on his promise to lower inflation.

The weak economic data extends beyond inflation. Overall gross domestic product growth was revised down to 1.6% in the first quarter from the previously estimated 2.0% pace. Consumer spending growth, which accounts for more than two-thirds of economic activity, was also revised downward.

The Federal Reserve will likely monitor inflation closely as it considers monetary policy decisions. However, policymakers face a difficult situation. Economic analysts note that while the Fed cannot fix a supply shock from the Middle East conflict, it cannot ignore one that is feeding into underlying inflation. Financial markets expect the Fed will hold its benchmark overnight interest rate steady well into 2027.

The combination of high inflation, slowing growth, and declining real incomes poses challenges for both households and policymakers as economic uncertainty persists.

cards.headline: Trump says he may not renew trade agreement with Mexico and Canada
cards.teaser: President Trump said he may not renew the free trade agreement between the U.S., Canada, and Mexico that he implemented in his first term.
cards.body:
President Trump indicated Wednesday that he may not seek to renew the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the trade deal he signed six years ago to replace the North American Free Trade Agreement during his first term.

The USMCA was considered a major achievement of Trump's earlier presidency, fundamentally restructuring trade relations among the three North American nations. His latest comments suggest a potential change in direction regarding the agreement he previously promoted as an improvement over NAFTA.

cards.headline: Trump calls for $350 billion defense spending increase in new GOP bill
cards.teaser: President Trump has requested a major Pentagon budget boost and election law changes in a third party-line reconciliation bill.
cards.body:
President Trump called on congressional Republicans to pass a third reconciliation bill that would increase Pentagon funding by $350 billion and include provisions from the Save America Act addressing election procedures. The proposed legislation would move through the budget reconciliation process, allowing passage with only Republican votes.

Top Republican appropriators pushed back against the proposal, with senior Senate defense and appropriations leaders stating that a third reconciliation bill is not feasible. The resistance from senior committee chairs suggests the proposal faces significant obstacles despite presidential backing.

cards.headline: Ukrainian missiles strike military plant deep inside Russia
cards.teaser: Ukraine launched long-range strikes against Russian military facilities, including targets in St. Petersburg.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces used Flamingo missiles to hit targets deep inside Russian territory. Strikes targeted a military plant far from the front lines, demonstrating Ukraine's expanding reach into Russian territory. Mass drone strikes also hit military facilities in St. Petersburg, one of Russia's most important cities.

Separate Ukrainian strikes set off fires at oil facilities in Russia and Crimea. The attacks inflict damage on Russian infrastructure and military production far from Ukrainian borders. The strikes represent Ukraine's growing ability to project force across long distances into Russian-controlled territory.

cards.headline: Russian ammunition chief killed in car bomb near Moscow
cards.teaser: A senior Russian military official died in a car explosion outside Moscow.
cards.body:
A car bomb killed a senior Russian military official near Moscow. The victim oversaw ammunition operations for the Russian military. Russian authorities have opened an investigation into the attack, which occurred in a fiery explosion that destroyed the vehicle.

The killing represents a targeted strike against Russia's military leadership. Reports indicate Russia is investigating two separate car bomb incidents in Moscow. The ammunition chief's death comes as Ukraine has intensified attacks on Russian military targets and infrastructure.

cards.headline: Cold spot in Atlantic Ocean may signal weakening of major current system
cards.teaser: Scientists identified an unusual cold region in the Atlantic that could indicate the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation is approaching a tipping point.
cards.body:
Researchers identified a cold region in the Atlantic Ocean that suggests the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation may be weakening. The AMOC is a system of ocean currents that moves warm water north and plays a major role in regulating climate across North America and Europe.

The cold blob appears in an ocean that is otherwise warming. Scientists consider this anomaly a potential indicator that the current system is slowing down, which could alter weather patterns across the United States and other regions. The findings contribute to ongoing research about climate tipping points and their potential impacts on global weather systems.

hero.headline: Police use water cannon as anti-immigrant violence spreads in Belfast
hero.teaser: A new wave of violence erupted in Belfast following a knife attack, prompting police to deploy water cannon.
hero.body:
A knife attack in Belfast triggered widespread disorder across the city and other parts of Northern Ireland. Police deployed water cannon after riot officers came under sustained attack from groups throwing bricks, bottles, and pieces of wood at a major roundabout in the northwest of Belfast.

Violence escalated as cars and a bus were set on fire, and families were forced to flee their homes. The disorder reflects a broader wave of anti-immigrant sentiment affecting the UK region as authorities worked to contain the situation.

cards.headline: Russian ammunition chief killed in car bomb near Moscow
cards.teaser: A senior Russian military official died in a car explosion outside Moscow.
cards.body:
A car bomb killed a senior Russian military official near Moscow. The victim oversaw ammunition operations for the Russian military. Russian authorities have opened an investigation into the attack, which occurred in a fiery explosion that destroyed the vehicle.

The killing represents a targeted strike against Russia's military leadership. Reports indicate Russia is investigating two separate car bomb incidents in Moscow. The ammunition chief's death comes as Ukraine has intensified attacks on Russian military targets and infrastructure.

cards.headline: Ukraine war passes World War I in duration
cards.teaser: The conflict in Ukraine has now lasted longer than the First World War.
cards.body:
The war in Ukraine has now lasted longer than World War I. Like the earlier conflict, the current war is characterized by grinding battles and the deployment of new military technologies that reshape how combat operates.

Ukraine has adapted to the conflict by increasingly relying on robotic warfare, including ground-based drones that handle frontline duties traditionally performed by soldiers. This technological shift allows Ukraine to maximize its military effectiveness on the battlefield.

cards.headline: Indonesian military court sentences four in acid attack on rights advocate
cards.teaser: A military court in Indonesia convicted four people in an acid attack against a critic of the armed forces.
cards.body:
An Indonesian military court sentenced four individuals for an acid attack on a human rights advocate. The victim has been an outspoken critic of Indonesia's military. Military prosecutors took control of the case over the victim's objections.

The case raised questions about accountability when military personnel face accusations of attacks on civilians. The victim opposed having the case heard in a military court rather than a civilian tribunal. The military court's jurisdiction over the case has drawn scrutiny from human rights observers.

cards.headline: Dispute emerges over cause of Air India flight 171 crash
cards.teaser: Investigators remain divided over what caused an Air India flight to crash.
cards.body:
A dispute has emerged among investigators examining the crash of Air India flight 171. Different parties involved in the investigation disagree over what caused the accident. The final conclusions have not yet been published, though more information may become clear in the coming days.

The disagreement underscores the challenge of investigating aviation accidents, which often requires analyzing multiple factors and weighing competing theories about what happened during the flight.

cards.headline: Everest guide's survival raises questions about tourism industry
cards.teaser: The rescue of an Everest guide who was working as a cook has prompted scrutiny of climbing operations.
cards.body:
An Everest guide survived after being left to rescue himself on the mountain. The individual was working as a cook but was leading clients up the peak. The incident has raised questions about safety practices and qualifications in the mountaineering tourism industry.

The case highlights concerns about who guides climbers on dangerous expeditions. The guide's dual role as cook and expedition leader, combined with being left to self-rescue, has prompted examination of industry standards and oversight on the world's highest mountain.

cards.headline: Federal judge warns Justice Department against reviving payout fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge has cautioned the Justice Department not to restart a controversial fund despite officials saying the program has been halted.
cards.body:
A federal judge has cautioned the Justice Department against attempting to restart the Anti-Weaponization Fund, a $1.8 billion program that the department says it has already discontinued. The judge stopped short of immediately blocking the fund, despite requests from watchdog groups concerned about its operation.

The ruling allows the fund to remain inactive while warning department officials that any effort to revive it would face legal challenges. The decision reflects ongoing tension between the Justice Department's claims that the program is no longer active and external pressure to ensure it stays permanently shuttered.

cards.headline: ActBlue CEO invokes Fifth Amendment during congressional hearing
cards.teaser: The chief executive of ActBlue repeatedly declined to answer questions from House panel members by citing Fifth Amendment protections.
cards.body:
The CEO of ActBlue appeared before a House committee and invoked Fifth Amendment rights multiple times when questioned by panel members. The hearing focused on an intensifying probe into donor fraud allegations involving the Democratic fundraising platform.

House Democrats responded to the investigation by threatening to target WinRed, the Republican fundraising counterpart, as the congressional inquiry continues. The ActBlue chief published an opinion piece explaining the decision to use Fifth Amendment protections during the testimony.

cards.headline: Trump calls for $350 billion defense spending increase in new GOP bill
cards.teaser: President Trump has requested a major Pentagon budget boost and election law changes in a third party-line reconciliation bill.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Suspect in Minnesota lawmaker killing reaches plea agreement
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors will not seek the death penalty after a suspect agreed to plead guilty in the killing of a Minnesota state legislator.
cards.body:
A man accused of killing a prominent Minnesota Democratic lawmaker has agreed to plead guilty as part of a deal with federal prosecutors. The suspect had previously pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Federal authorities will not seek the death penalty under the plea agreement. The case drew significant federal attention due to its classification as a political killing, making it a high-profile prosecution.

cards.headline: Karmelo Anthony files appeal one day after 35-year murder sentence
cards.teaser: Lawyers for a Texas man convicted of murder at a track meet filed an appeal notice immediately after he received a 35-year prison term.
cards.body:
Karmelo Anthony was sentenced to 35 years in prison for murder in a stabbing case that occurred at a Texas track meet. His legal team filed a notice of appeal one day after the sentencing, with Anthony stating he cannot afford a lawyer for the appeal process.

The case became a focal point of controversy, with public figures including Cardi B criticizing the conviction. Anthony's parents have characterized the trial as unfair, while the teenage stabbing case has drawn attention as what some describe as a racial flashpoint in Texas.

cards.headline: US conducts second night of airstrikes on Iranian targets
cards.teaser: American forces bombed military sites in southern Iran for the second consecutive night as diplomatic efforts continue.
cards.body:
The United States carried out a second consecutive night of strikes against military targets in southern Iran. In response, Iran targeted US military assets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan, escalating the exchange of military action across the Middle East.

The strikes prompted regional responses, with Kuwait closing its airspace and Israel issuing warnings about potential launches from Lebanon. During the operations, a sea drone rescued a US Army helicopter crew near the Strait of Hormuz.

hero.headline: Trump Says He 'Loves the Inflation' as Consumer Prices Rise at Fastest Rate in Three Years
hero.teaser: President Trump made the statement as new data showed inflation accelerating amid the U.S.-Israel war in Iran.
hero.body:
President Trump stated he loves the inflation after new data showed consumer prices jumped to 4.2% annually in May, the highest rate in three years. The surge marks the third consecutive monthly increase since the U.S. and Israel launched military operations against Iran. Speaking from the White House, Trump said he was not concerned about the rising prices given recent developments in the conflict.

Inflation had stood at 2.4% before the Iran war began. The escalation in consumer prices has been driven largely by surging gasoline costs following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which affects energy supplies and prices across the economy.

cards.headline: Global Stock Markets Retreat as Tech Stocks Extend Losses and U.S. Strikes Iran
cards.teaser: Asian and European shares fell following another selloff in technology stocks and renewed Middle East military action.
cards.body:
Stock markets declined across Asia and Europe as technology stocks extended their losses. The selloff followed developments in the Middle East, where the U.S. and Iran exchanged military strikes for a second consecutive day. U.S. forces targeted military sites in southern Iran, while Tehran responded by firing on American military assets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan.

Oil prices climbed amid concerns about potential supply disruptions from the escalating conflict. The geopolitical tensions contributed to broader market weakness, with investors reacting to both the Middle East situation and ongoing weakness in the technology sector.

cards.headline: Dow Jones Futures Rise as Markets Digest Middle East Strikes and Corporate Earnings
cards.teaser: Stock futures climbed while oil prices increased following U.S. military action against Iran.
cards.body:
Dow Jones futures rose in early trading as investors assessed the U.S. completion of strikes against Iran's military targets. The exchange of fire between the two countries marked the second consecutive day of direct military action, intensifying concerns about potential escalation. Oil prices climbed on heightened supply worries stemming from the Middle East tensions.

Corporate developments also shaped market sentiment, with Oracle shares declining while SpaceX moved closer to launching an initial public offering. The futures gains followed a challenging session for the Dow, which had fallen 800 points amid inflation concerns and geopolitical risks, with technology stocks particularly pressured.

cards.headline: Frasers Group Offers £1.73 Billion to Buy All of Hugo Boss
cards.teaser: Mike Ashley's retail group already owns just over a quarter of the German fashion brand.
cards.body:
Frasers Group, controlled by Mike Ashley, has made a £1.73 billion offer to acquire all remaining shares of Hugo Boss. The retail group already owns just over a quarter of the German fashion brand and is seeking to buy out the rest.

The bid would give Frasers complete ownership of one of Germany's leading fashion brands.

cards.headline: Lee Raymond, Former Exxon Mobil Chief Who Created Oil Giant, Dies at 87
cards.teaser: Raymond oversaw Exxon's acquisition of Mobil and became known for denying the scientific consensus on climate change.
cards.body:
Lee Raymond, the former chief executive of Exxon Mobil, has died at age 87. Raymond orchestrated the landmark merger between Exxon and Mobil that created one of the world's largest oil companies. Under his leadership, he implemented sweeping cost reductions and expanded the company's global reach.

Raymond was a prominent public voice questioning the scientific consensus on climate change, a position that drew sustained opposition from environmental groups and the scientific community during his career.

cards.headline: Anthropic Reverses Policy After Backlash from AI Researchers Using Claude
cards.teaser: The company walked back restrictions on its Fable model that could have disrupted cybersecurity research.
cards.body:
Anthropic released Fable 5, the first widely available model from its new Mythos class of AI technology, on Tuesday. The company had restricted access to Fable 5 for months following its April unveiling due to cybersecurity concerns, limiting it to a small group of partner institutions.

The public release comes with restrictions on the model's use in sensitive areas. This move represents a shift in Anthropic's approach to balancing safety considerations with broader access to its most advanced AI capabilities.

cards.headline: Medicare Advantage Plans Frequently Deny Seniors Access to Nursing Home Care, Analysis Finds
cards.teaser: Two federal reports show the plans quickly reject requests for short-term nursing home or inpatient rehabilitation services.
cards.body:
Medicare Advantage plans often deny seniors access to specialized care, according to two reports by U.S. investigators. The analysis revealed that the private insurance plans are quick to reject requests for short-term nursing home stays or inpatient rehabilitation services.

The findings raise questions about how Medicare Advantage, which has grown rapidly as an alternative to traditional Medicare, manages access to post-acute care. The reports document patterns of denials that may limit seniors' ability to receive necessary medical services after hospitalizations or injuries.

hero.headline: Apple updates Siri with voice activity detection and new foundation models
hero.body:
Apple unveiled a substantially redesigned Siri at its annual developer conference, marking a major shift in the voice assistant's capabilities. The new Siri, rebranded as "Siri AI," integrates with Apple Intelligence and will be widely available in the fall.

The revamped assistant represents a fundamental reconception of how Siri functions. Rather than operating as a web-based question-and-answer tool, the updated version mimics modern AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Google Gemini. Mike Rockwell, Apple's vice-president of Siri engineering, demonstrated the assistant's new conversational abilities during the conference, showing how it can work across Apple's native app ecosystem to handle tasks like planning, navigation and information retrieval.

A key advancement enables Siri to operate within a single interface rather than shuffling between multiple apps. In a demonstration, Rockwell showed Siri identifying a beach location from a photo, retrieving a friend's address from the contact app, and providing directions to the beach with a stop at the friend's house, all without leaving the Siri interface.

The new Siri will feature its own dedicated app and can handle expanded functionality including proofreading, shopping, calendar management and extracting information from images using the camera. Initially, English will be the only supported language.

Apple achieved these improvements through a partnership with Google, leveraging Google's Gemini AI model. According to Dipanjan Chatterjee, a principal analyst at Forrester, this represents a significant moment for Apple. He noted that "a fundamentally re-architected Siri inside iOS 27 with a little help from Google's Gemini would represent more than an update – it would signal Apple's readiness to make AI the primary interface layer across its ecosystem."

The update comes after years of delays and false starts with Siri improvements. Apple had previously postponed releasing an updated version first announced in 2024, as its AI development lagged competitors. The company faced additional pressure from a 250 million dollar settlement in May following a class-action lawsuit alleging false advertising of Siri's AI capabilities.

Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice-president of software engineering, acknowledged during the conference that some companies appear to be "racing forward, seemingly pursuing AI for the sake of AI, without clear regard for the people." This framing positions Apple's approach as more deliberately integrated into existing products rather than pursuing AI as a standalone technology.

Beyond Siri, Apple announced new AI features across Safari, messaging and the Home app, alongside camera and photo tools developed with Google. The company also introduced expanded child safety features allowing parents greater control over content access and app usage through an updated setup assistant and monitoring tools.

cards.headline: Former xAI engineer sues over alleged firing for raising Grok safety concerns
cards.teaser: A former employee claims he was terminated after flagging AI safety issues with Grok shortly before SpaceX's initial public offering.
cards.body:
A former xAI engineer has filed a lawsuit against xAI and SpaceX, claiming he was terminated in retaliation for raising safety concerns about Grok, the company's AI system. The firing allegedly occurred days before SpaceX's initial public offering.

The engineer contends that his dismissal was retaliatory, directly tied to the internal warnings he had raised regarding Grok's safety protocols and potential risks.

cards.headline: Hackers claim breach of Oracle PeopleSoft servers at over 100 organizations
cards.teaser: The ShinyHunters hacking group says it compromised Oracle PeopleSoft servers across multiple universities and other institutions.
cards.body:
The ShinyHunters hacking gang has claimed responsibility for compromising Oracle PeopleSoft servers across more than 100 organizations, with universities among the affected institutions. Oracle PeopleSoft is an enterprise software platform used widely for managing human resources, financial operations, and supply chain functions at large organizations.

ShinyHunters has a history of claiming responsibility for data breaches at multiple companies and has been associated with selling stolen information obtained through these compromises.

cards.headline: Florida man sues police over arrest based on facial recognition match
cards.teaser: The lawsuit argues that officers relied on a 93 percent facial recognition match instead of conducting a proper investigation.
cards.body:
Robert Dillon was arrested at his Florida home despite living 300 miles away from where a crime occurred. Police used facial recognition software that returned a 93 percent match identifying him as a man seen on security cameras at a McDonald's attempting to persuade an unaccompanied child to leave with him.

Dillon is suing multiple law enforcement agencies over the arrest and prosecution. The lawsuit challenges law enforcement's reliance on algorithmic matches without corroborating evidence, arguing the technology is error-prone and should not substitute for thorough investigation.

cards.teaser: Scientists identified an unusual cold region in the Atlantic that could indicate the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation is approaching a tipping point.

cards.headline: Study finds humans consistently prefer walking in counterclockwise circles
cards.teaser: Researchers documented a widespread tendency for pedestrians to move counterclockwise in crowds, though the cause remains unknown.
cards.body:
Scientists published research in Nature showing that humans have an inherent preference for counterclockwise motion when walking in groups or circular patterns. The study documented this behavior across different populations and settings, revealing a consistent bias in how people navigate spaces.

Researchers found that individual locomotor bias drives the counterclockwise motion in pedestrian crowds. The team has not identified a clear explanation for why this preference exists, though they ruled out several potential causes. The findings could have applications in crowd management and urban design.

cards.headline: Rain event decimated population of world's rarest orangutans, researchers say
cards.teaser: A study linked climate change-induced weather to a significant decline in orangutan numbers over just four days.
cards.body:
Four days of extreme rainfall in Indonesia's North Sumatra province killed 58 critically endangered Tapanuli orangutans in November 2025. The downpour exceeded 1,000mm and triggered landslides that devastated the species. This represents 7% of the world's remaining population of roughly 800 individuals.

The deaths underscore the vulnerability of the world's rarest great ape to climate-driven weather extremes. Researchers linked the disaster to the climate crisis, raising concerns about the species' survival as it already faces habitat loss and other environmental pressures.

hero.headline: Knicks rally from 25 points down to beat Spurs, take 3-1 NBA Finals lead
hero.body:
The New York Knicks completed the largest comeback in NBA Finals history, erasing a 29-point deficit to defeat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 in Game 4 on Wednesday night. OG Anunoby's tip-in with 2.3 seconds remaining proved decisive, giving New York a commanding 3-1 series lead and putting them one win away from their first championship in 53 years.

The Spurs dominated much of the game, building their substantial lead as Victor Wembanyama controlled stretches of play. San Antonio's advantage appeared insurmountable as the Knicks fell further behind, but New York mounted an extraordinary rally in the second half that shocked the Madison Square Garden crowd.

Jalen Brunson led the Knicks' comeback effort, scoring 32 points and hitting crucial shots down the stretch. Anunoby added 28 points during the regular season but delivered the game-winner when it mattered most. Brunson's missed three-pointer on the final possession provided Anunoby with the opportunity for the winning tip-in.

The game featured intense physical play between the teams. Wembanyama was involved in multiple flagrant foul incidents with Knicks players Karl-Anthony Towns and Mitchell Robinson. The French center drew some calls while committing others, though disagreements over the officiating emerged as the contest wore on. The Knicks believed they received unfavorable treatment from referees, particularly in the fourth quarter when San Antonio attempted significantly more free throws.

The atmosphere at Madison Square Garden reflected the magnitude of the occasion. The game marked New York's first NBA Finals contest at home since 1999. Notable attendees included President Donald Trump, who received heavy boos when shown on the jumbotron during the national anthem. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani also attended, having purchased a standing-room-only ticket for approximately one thousand dollars. Celebrities including Spike Lee, Timothée Chalamet, Ben Stiller, and Larry David sat courtside.

The comeback overshadowed the pre-game drama surrounding the event. A watch party had been cancelled amid a public dispute involving Knicks ownership, and the NYPD imposed restrictions on spontaneous gatherings outside the arena ahead of tipoff.

San Antonio now faces elimination as the series shifts back to their home court. The Spurs must win three consecutive games to capture the championship, a feat no team has accomplished after falling behind 3-1 in the Finals. Wembanyama and his teammates must regroup quickly to extend the series and avoid squandering their home court advantage.

For the Knicks and their fanbase, the historic victory represents a remarkable opportunity to end the franchise's 53-year championship drought with a victory in Game 5.

cards.headline: Chiefs give Patrick Mahomes record $504.75 million deal through 2033
cards.teaser: The Kansas City Chiefs restructured quarterback Patrick Mahomes' contract, creating the first NFL deal valued at over $500 million.
cards.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have restructured Patrick Mahomes' contract, adding two years and pushing his total compensation to $504.75 million. The deal ties the quarterback to the franchise through the 2033 season, when he will be 38 years old. Incentives and escalators could raise the value beyond $520 million.

Mahomes originally signed a 10-year, $450 million contract with Kansas City in 2020, which set a benchmark for NFL players. The latest restructuring extends that agreement and makes him the highest-paid player in league history.

cards.headline: Big Ten considers league-wide ban on scheduling Texas Tech over Brendan Sorsby ruling
cards.teaser: Conference officials are discussing a potential scheduling boycott of Texas Tech across all sports following a court decision regarding quarterback Brendan Sorsby.
cards.body:
The Big Ten Conference is considering implementing a league-wide ban on scheduling Texas Tech in all sports, according to reports from The Athletic and The New York Times. The potential action comes in response to a Texas judge's ruling involving quarterback Brendan Sorsby that has drawn backlash from coaches and athletic directors around the country.

Texas Tech booster Cody Campbell responded to the controversy by threatening lawsuits against the College Football Playoff and warning other conferences against avoiding scheduling the Red Raiders. Campbell stated that opponents "don't want to play us," defending the school's position. Coaches and athletic directors from other programs have described their reactions to the Sorsby ruling as "disgusted" and "stunned," with opinion pieces calling it the biggest scandal in college sports.

cards.headline: UFC Freedom 250 event set for White House with President Trump in attendance
cards.teaser: The UFC will hold its Freedom 250 event at the White House, with fighters expressing honor at competing in front of the president.
cards.body:
The UFC is preparing to hold Freedom 250, an unprecedented event at the White House with President Trump scheduled to attend. Fighters arriving for the event have stated they feel honored to compete on the card in front of the president, marking an innovation in UFC history alongside other notable ventures like Fight Island.

The event represents a first for the organization, bringing mixed martial arts to the White House grounds. Full fight card details, dates, odds, and viewing information have been released for the Freedom 250 card. The president's attendance has drawn significant attention to the event, though Trump has maintained a relatively low profile as fighters have arrived and prepared for their bouts.

cards.headline: NCAA outdoor track and field championships underway in Eugene
cards.teaser: The 2026 Division I outdoor track and field championships are in progress, with multiple athletes advancing to finals.
cards.body:
The NCAA Division I outdoor track and field championships are taking place in Eugene, Oregon, with competition underway across multiple events. Day 1 results showed the Florida Gators positioned to compete for trophies, while several other programs saw their athletes advance to championship finals.

Four Michigan Wolverines advanced to finals in their respective events, with one athlete earning Second Team All-American honors. Live results and updates are being provided throughout the competition as athletes compete for individual and team titles. The championships represent the culmination of the outdoor track season for collegiate athletes across the country.

cards.headline: England manager Thomas Tuchel faces lineup decisions ahead of World Cup opener against Croatia
cards.teaser: With World Cup preparations complete, England's manager must finalize his starting XI, including whether to field Jude Bellingham at number 10 and Bukayo Saka.
cards.body:
England manager Thomas Tuchel says his squad is ready for the World Cup after a convincing 3-0 warm-up victory over Costa Rica in Orlando. Declan Rice, Anthony Gordon and Ollie Watkins scored as England overcame a one-hour weather delay to secure the win.

Jude Bellingham impressed in the match alongside Kane, putting him in contention to start in the opening Group L fixture against Croatia in Dallas next Wednesday. Tuchel expressed satisfaction with how his team responded to the disruption and believes they are well-positioned for their tournament campaign.

cards.headline: Storm delay halts England-Costa Rica match amid extreme weather concerns
cards.teaser: England's match against Costa Rica was postponed due to extreme weather, raising questions about climate conditions during the World Cup.
cards.body:
A match between England and Costa Rica was delayed after extreme weather forced officials to halt play. The incident has prompted discussion about whether such weather disruptions could become more common during the World Cup tournament.

The delay comes as the World Cup faces scrutiny over organizational challenges. The postponement due to severe storms has raised concerns about how weather patterns might affect the competition schedule and whether tournament organizers adequately prepared for climate-related disruptions during the event.

hero.headline: 24 Jump Street in Development With Original Stars in Talks to Return
hero.body:
A third installment in the Jump Street comedy franchise is in development, with Jonah Hill, Channing Tatum, and Ice Cube in talks to return for 24 Jump Street. The project marks a return to the series that began with 21 Jump Street in 2012 and continued with 22 Jump Street in 2014.

The original films followed two undercover cops, played by Hill and Tatum, as they infiltrated high school and college to investigate drug rings. Ice Cube portrayed their commanding officer. The movies became critical and commercial successes, with 21 Jump Street earning over $200 million worldwide and 22 Jump Street surpassing $330 million globally. Both films were praised for their chemistry between the leads and their blend of action and comedy.

Tatum has been publicly pushing for a third film for years. The actor previously expressed his desire to bring the franchise back, and his persistence appears to have paid off. The development of 24 Jump Street comes more than a decade after the last installment, making it one of the longest gaps between sequels in the series.

No director has been announced for the project, though Phil Lord and Christopher Miller directed the first two films. The previous installments were produced by Columbia Pictures and distributed by Sony Pictures. Details about the plot and production timeline have not been disclosed.

The Jump Street franchise originated as a reboot of the 1987 television series of the same name, which launched Johnny Depp's career. The films successfully transformed the source material into a comedic take on the buddy cop genre, earning praise for self-awareness and humor. The return of the original cast would continue the story of the partnership between Hill and Tatum's characters, whose dynamic anchored both previous films.

cards.headline: BIGBANG Announces 31-Show World Stadium Tour for 20th Anniversary
cards.teaser: The K-pop group will bring G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung together for shows across Asia, North America, Europe, and Australia.
cards.body:
BIGBANG has announced a 31-show world stadium tour to celebrate the group's 20th anniversary. The tour will reunite G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung for performances across four continents, spanning Asia, North America, Europe, and Australia.

The announcement marks a significant moment for the K-pop pioneers, who have been credited with shaping the genre's global expansion. The tour represents one of the largest undertakings by the group, with stadium venues indicating the scale of their continued international appeal two decades into their career.

cards.headline: Wu-Tang Clan Performs at NBA Finals Halftime Show
cards.teaser: The Staten Island hip-hop group performed during halftime of Game 4 as the Spurs held a large lead over the Knicks.
cards.body:
Wu-Tang Clan took the court at Madison Square Garden for the halftime show during Game 4 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs. The Staten Island natives performed as the Spurs entered the third quarter holding a significant lead over the home team.

The performance brought the legendary hip-hop group to one of basketball's biggest stages. Wu-Tang Clan, formed in New York in the early 1990s, has remained one of the most influential groups in hip-hop history. Their appearance at the Finals connected their New York roots with the city's basketball culture during a high-stakes championship series.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Attends NBA Finals Game at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The singer attended Game 4 of the Knicks-Spurs series, wearing a Stevie Knicks shirt alongside the Haim sisters.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift was among the celebrities courtside at Madison Square Garden for Game 4 of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs. She watched the Knicks orchestrate a remarkable comeback, pulling off the largest turnaround in NBA Finals history with a 29-point swing to secure a 107-106 victory.

The game drew numerous high-profile attendees to the iconic arena, including Spike Lee, Adam Sandler, Ben Stiller, Timothée Chalamet, and others. With the victory, the Knicks took a 3-1 series lead in the best-of-seven matchup against the Spurs.

cards.headline: Kylie Jenner and Timothée Chalamet Wear Matching Denim to NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The couple appeared courtside at Game 4 in custom Knicks-themed denim outfits by Chrome Hearts.
cards.body:
Kylie Jenner and Timothée Chalamet attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden wearing coordinating denim outfits. The couple wore custom Knicks-themed denim pieces by Chrome Hearts and were photographed holding hands at the game.

Chalamet, a known Knicks fan, and Jenner sat courtside for the matchup between New York and San Antonio. The matching looks featured denim in support of the home team during the high-profile Finals game, which drew numerous celebrities to the Manhattan arena.

cards.headline: Celebrities Fill Courtside Seats for Knicks NBA Finals Game
cards.teaser: Spike Lee, Adam Sandler, Ben Stiller, Larry David, and others watched the Knicks mount a historic comeback against the Spurs.
cards.body:
Madison Square Garden's courtside was packed with A-list celebrities as the New York Knicks faced the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4 of the NBA Finals. Spike Lee, Adam Sandler, Ben Stiller, Larry David, and Timothée Chalamet were among the notable attendees supporting the home team.

The Knicks delivered a stunning performance, completing a 29-point comeback—the largest in NBA Finals history—to defeat the Spurs 107-106. The victory gave New York a 3-1 series lead in the best-of-seven championship matchup, underscoring the cultural significance of the team's Finals run.

cards.headline: JioHotstar's Microdrama Platform Tadka Reaches 100 Million Users
cards.teaser: The short-form content platform within India's leading streamer has seen daily watch time per viewer grow fivefold since launch.
cards.body:
Tadka, the microdrama platform within Indian streaming service JioHotstar, has surpassed 100 million users. Daily watch time per viewer has grown fivefold since the platform launched, and more than 42 percent of viewers are under age 24.

The milestone establishes premium short-form content as a mainstream entertainment category in India. Tadka operates within JioHotstar, one of India's largest streaming platforms, and focuses on microdramas, which are episodic stories told in short installments. The platform's growth reflects changing viewing habits among younger audiences in the Indian market.

hero.headline: U.S. launches second night of airstrikes on Iran to pressure nuclear deal
hero.body:
The U.S. military struck targets in Iran for the second consecutive night, with officials stating the intent was to pressure Tehran to sign a nuclear agreement. The strikes carry the risk of escalating military conflict between the two countries.

U.S. officials said they expected an Iranian response, similar to what occurred after the first round of strikes. Tehran announced its military had targeted the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet in Bahrain with drones in response to the latest American strikes, though it was not immediately clear whether the attack succeeded.

The sequential nights of bombing represent an intensification of U.S. military action against Iran. Officials framed the operation as part of a strategy to bring Iran to the negotiating table for an agreement, though the approach risks provoking further retaliation against American forces in the region.

The 5th Fleet, headquartered in Bahrain, oversees U.S. naval operations in the Persian Gulf, Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and parts of the Indian Ocean. Iranian drone attacks targeting the fleet would represent a direct military response to American forces, raising the prospect of an expanding conflict. U.S. bases in the region have previously been targeted by Iranian forces and allied militias.

The back-and-forth strikes mark a significant moment in U.S.-Iran relations, with both countries engaged in direct military action against each other. The outcome of the pressure campaign remains uncertain, as does Iran's capacity and willingness to continue retaliatory strikes against American military installations in response to the ongoing air operations.

cards.headline: Trump calls for immediate passage of $350 billion reconciliation bill
cards.teaser: President Trump endorsed a third reconciliation bill and urged Congress to pass it immediately with the Save America Act included.
cards.body:
President Trump called on Republicans in Congress to immediately advance and pass a forthcoming $350 billion reconciliation bill. The president requested the legislation include the Save America Act.

Trump made the announcement publicly, referring to the measure as Recon 3.0. The bill was prepared at the request of the Department of War, according to the president's statement.

cards.headline: Trump says he may not renew trade agreement with Mexico and Canada
cards.teaser: President Trump said he may not renew the free trade agreement between the U.S., Canada, and Mexico that he implemented in his first term.
cards.body:
President Trump indicated Wednesday that he may not seek to renew the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, the trade deal he signed six years ago to replace the North American Free Trade Agreement during his first term.

The USMCA was considered a major achievement of Trump's earlier presidency, fundamentally restructuring trade relations among the three North American nations. His latest comments suggest a potential change in direction regarding the agreement he previously promoted as an improvement over NAFTA.

cards.headline: Schumer criticizes Trump administration as inflation reaches 4.2 percent
cards.teaser: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer attacked the Trump administration after new data showed consumer prices increased 4.2 percent over the last year.
cards.body:
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer criticized the Trump administration after Labor Department data showed the consumer price index rose 4.2 percent over the last year, with a 0.5 percent increase in May alone. Schumer used the term "Trumpflation" to describe what he characterized as worsening inflation rates under the current administration.

The inflation spike represents a three-year high, following three consecutive monthly increases since the start of the Iran war. Prior to the conflict, inflation had been at 2.4 percent, but the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has affected energy prices.

cards.headline: Agriculture secretary rejects Grassley call for screwworm vaccine
cards.teaser: Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley urged Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins to create a vaccine for New World screwworms after the parasite returned to the U.S.
cards.body:
Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley pressed Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins to develop a vaccine for New World screwworms after the parasite returned to the United States for the first time in six decades. An outbreak emerged in Texas, prompting Grassley's push for action.

Rollins rejected the suggestion. Grassley said he had raised the vaccine proposal with Rollins months before the recent outbreak occurred. The senator chairs the Judiciary Committee, which typically does not oversee agricultural matters.

cards.headline: NASA chief defends all-male crew for Artemis III mission
cards.teaser: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman defended the decision to use an all-male crew for the Artemis III mission despite the space program being named after a Greek goddess.
cards.body:
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman responded to criticism over the all-male crew selection for Artemis III, acknowledging on social media that he had seen reactions ranging from disappointment to outrage regarding the lack of female astronauts.

The Artemis III mission is scheduled to launch in 2027. The crew includes NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas, along with Luca Parmitano from the European Space Agency. They will orbit Earth while practicing docking procedures with lunar landers in preparation for the eventual Moon landing.

cards.headline: House Democrats struggle to collect member dues to campaign committee
cards.teaser: More than half of House Democrats had paid less than 50 percent of their expected dues to the party's campaign committee as of early April.
cards.body:
More than half of House Democrats had paid less than 50 percent of their expected dues to the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee as of early April, according to a member dues report. The average payment rate stood at 47 percent.

Nearly 30 members who are not in battleground districts have paid nothing. The dues issue comes as some House Democrats threaten to withhold payments unless the DCCC stops intervening in primaries. While not the committee's only source of income, member dues represent a significant funding stream.
